It is an appeal filed by the insurance company aggrieved by the order passed by II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional CFECT-III, Chitradurga in ECA.No.25/2015 dated 3rd of January 2017.

sentences.text: 2. The petition is filed under Section 22 of the employees Compensation Act seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.15,00,000/- for the death of the deceased who died during the employment.
According to the claimants the deceased was working under the Respondent No.1 as driver of the lorry since one year prior to the date of accident.
The deceased had been engaged as driver from Chitradurga to Hospete to unload iron ore.

When the lorry came near Chikkagondanahally gate, the deceased being driver of the said lorry had lost his control and dashed to road side bridge, as a result the lorry toppled down and the driver i.e., the deceased sustained injuries to his head, abdomen and died at the spot.

3. It is the case of the insurance company that the deceased was responsible for the accident and charge NC: 2023:KHC:33756 sheet had been filed under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC and under Section 3 of MV Act.
They have issued a notice to the claimants as well as the owner of the vehicle to produce the driving license.
As the driver was not having valid driving license, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

The Court below had granted compensation of an amount of Rs.6,24,000/- but when it comes to the liability the Court below had observed that, just because a charge sheet is filed under Section 3 of the MV Act that itself cannot be a ground.

Further,
Court to came to the conclusion that there was no driving license.
The Court below observed that the insurance company had failed to prove the same by adducing the evidence and held that the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.
Aggrieved thereby the insurance company is before this Court.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the insurance company relying on the judgment of the Apex Court in NC: 2023:KHC:33756 BELI RAM V/S. RAJINDER KUMAR REPORTED1 submits that, as he is a workman and claims to be a driver, it is the obligation on the part of the claimants to place the driving license before the Court and the charge sheet filed against the deceased also shows that there is no driving license.

entities.text: NC: 2023:KHC:33756 BELI RAM V/S. RAJINDER KUMAR
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that in these circumstances, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
The said aspect was not considered by the Tribunal.

5. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the workman has relied on the order passed by the Apex Court in case of GURMAIL SINGH V/S. BAJAJ ALLIANZ GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD.2 and he submits that, in the said case, though there was no driving license, the Apex court has permitted the claimants to recover the amount from the insurer and gave liberty to the insurer to recover the same in turn from the owner of the vehicle.

entities.text: GURMAIL SINGH V/S. BAJAJ ALLIANZ GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD.2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The material on record reveals that there is no driving license.
The Court below went wrong in giving a conclusion that, the insurer had failed to prove the same.

When it is the case of the claimants that the deceased was a workman discharging his duties as a driver the burden lies on them to place the driving license on record, the crime that was registered under Section 3 of the MV Act also strengthens the case of the insurance company.

7. Accordingly, the appeal of the insurance company is allowed.

ii. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
iii. No costs.
